trouble_embedder: Search says the embedder isn't running
trouble_embedder_shows: “The embedder isn’t running. Quit Unseen Servant and open it again to search.” · “Embedder isn’t running. Search waits for it” · “Embedder didn’t answer. Search waits for it”
trouble_embedder_fix: The embedder starts with Unseen Servant and takes a few seconds to load its model. If it stays down, quit Unseen Servant and open it again. If it fails again, reinstall the app, and send {#em}llama-server.log{/em} from the data folder with your report (below).
trouble_index_fix: Hover that line in the status bar for each book's reason. {#em}Empty or scanned PDF{/em} means its pages are pictures with no text: run it through an OCR tool, then tick it again. A locked or damaged PDF fails the same way. If every book failed at once, the embedder is likely down (above).
trouble_weak: Search finds nothing, or only weak matches
trouble_weak_shows: “Everything is muted.” · “Nothing indexed is playing.” · “Nothing under the soloed items.” · “No strong matches — the content may be outside the current scope.”
trouble_weak_fix: A playing collection, a solo or a mute is narrowing the search. The {#strong}B{/strong} switch on the scope bar ({#strong}B{/strong} outside a text field) sets them all aside until you throw it back. Faded rows are weak matches; {#em}Settings → General → Dim weak matches{/em} turns the fading off.
trouble_mcp: The AI agent can't reach the library
trouble_mcp_shows: “MCP not detected” on the status bar lamp · the agent says “Cannot connect to Unseen Servant”
trouble_mcp_fix: Unseen Servant has to be running: closing its window doesn't quit it, quitting does. Check the config is in the agent's MCP settings (Help → Guides → Servant) and restart the agent after any edit. If the app moved since you copied the config, copy it again: the config holds the app's location.
trouble_offline_shows: “Sidecar didn’t start. Search and indexing are offline” · “Library store didn’t open” · “Indexer failed to start. See log: …”
trouble_offline_fix: Quit Unseen Servant and open it again; a first launch after installing can be slow. If it fails again, copy {#em}sidecar.log{/em} out of the data folder before reopening, as every launch starts a new one, and send it with your report (below).
trouble_library: The library folder can't be reached
trouble_library_shows: “Library folder isn’t reachable: …” · “Library folder is no longer accessible: …” · “Library folder isn’t responding: …”
trouble_library_fix: Connect the drive or network share it lives on. If the folder moved, choose it again in {#em}Settings → Library{/em}. On macOS, also check that {#em}System Settings → Privacy & Security → Files and Folders{/em} lets Unseen Servant in.
trouble_campaigns_fix: Connect the drive it lives on, or pick the folder again in {#em}Settings → Command{/em} (on macOS, also {#em}File → Change Campaigns Folder…{/em}).
trouble_stuck_fix: Write with what you see, and {#em}sidecar.log{/em} if search or indexing is involved.

lore_general_rerank_desc: Rescores the top candidates with a cross-encoder for a more accurate ordering. Strong impact on relevance, but also performance. Turn off if search is deemed too slow.
lore_general_pool_desc: How many candidates the re-ranker rescores. Deeper reaches further into the library but slows every search down.
lore_general_spell_desc: Fixes typos against your library's own vocabulary before searching.
lore_general_hybrid_desc: Adds exact-keyword (BM25) matches to semantic results. Helps rare names and exact terms.
lore_start_folder_desc: The folder that holds your PDFs. They are read where they are, nothing is uploaded or copied, and subfolders become the tree. Rename books and folders here ({#strong}R{/strong}) to keep their index; outside the app, a moved book or a renamed folder has to be indexed again.
lore_start_folder_images: Images in it (maps, handouts) show in the tree too, never indexed: right-click one and {#em}Send to Command{/em} copies it into the open campaign. {#em}Hide images{/em} in the filters takes them out of the tree.
lore_start_index_desc: Tick books or folders in the tree; the status bar then offers {#em}sync{/em} ({#strong}⌘S{/strong}). Later syncs index only the books that changed.
lore_start_collections_desc: Named sets of books. Play one (▶ or {#strong}P{/strong}) and search covers only its books; play several to search them together. Without a collection, solo ({#strong}S{/strong}) or mute ({#strong}M{/strong}) books and folders in the tree.
lore_start_collections_arm: {#strong}⌘N{/strong} starts one, armed (●): click books in the tree to file them in it, then disarm it with its ● or {#strong}E{/strong}. Dropping a book or folder on a collection files it too.
lore_status_bypass_title: Scope bypassed — every indexed file is in scope. B restores it.

command_guide_campaigns_desc: Each campaign is a folder in it: {#em}Unseen Servant{/em} in your home folder until you choose another in {#em}Settings → Command{/em}. Command reopens the campaign you used last; its key in the bar switches campaigns or starts a new one.
command_guide_tracks_desc: A campaign's folders are its tracks (PCs, Secrets, Locations, NPCs…), shown as columns, and each note is a Markdown file in one, so Obsidian reads the same folder. {#em}[[Name]]{/em} links one note to another. The shelf ({#strong}⌘B{/strong}) holds what isn't filed yet, such as a Legend Lore result sent with right-click › {#em}Send to Command{/em}.
command_guide_beats_desc: A beat is a scene: the notes it needs. Double-click the empty row of the session planner, on the right, to name one, or press {#strong}⇧⌘N{/strong}; it starts armed (●), so clicking notes puts them in it, and {#strong}Esc{/strong} disarms it. The selected row answers the keys a Legend Lore row does: {#strong}↓{/strong} and {#strong}↑{/strong} walk its list and {#strong}→{/strong} and {#strong}←{/strong} the tracks, {#strong}⌘⌥←{/strong} and {#strong}→{/strong} move between the shelf, the tracks and the beats, {#strong}E{/strong} arms a beat, {#strong}X{/strong} puts a note in the armed one, {#strong}↵{/strong} opens it, {#strong}R{/strong} renames it, {#strong}⌘N{/strong} starts a note in its track, {#strong}⌘⌫{/strong} moves it to the Trash. {#em}New session{/em} in the bar starts a session; drag beats into its plan.
command_guide_play_desc: {#strong}Tab{/strong} switches to Play, where the board holds the plan's notes as cards. In the session player, {#strong}P{/strong} or ▶ launches the focused beat and lights its cards; a card's ▶ puts one more note in play. The card tray under the board holds what's in play: point at a card to read all of it, or right-click cards to stand them up over the board and read them side by side, the tray folded under them; click or right-click a nameplate for another. Right-click a standing card to put it back, or press {#strong}Esc{/strong} or click the board to put them all back. A click on a card opens its menu, and a double-click its note; drag a card along the tray to put it in another place. {#strong}A{/strong} marks the note or beat under the pointer spent (a secret told, an NPC dead), and it stays dimmed in later sessions.
command_guide_tools_desc: The toolbar on the board's right edge arranges it before the session. {#strong}D{/strong} places any note of the campaign where you click, by name. {#strong}T{/strong} adds a text card and {#strong}N{/strong} a sticky where you click. {#strong}F{/strong} draws a frame, which carries the cards inside it when you move it; {#strong}⌘G{/strong} frames the selected cards. {#strong}L{/strong} draws a line from one card to another. Double-click a text card, a frame's name or a line to write in it. {#strong}H{/strong} pans over the cards, {#strong}V{/strong} or {#strong}Esc{/strong} goes back to selecting, and {#strong}⌘Z{/strong} undoes.
command_guide_tools_select: Select a sticky, a text card, a frame or a line to colour it from the bar over it; a line's bar also sets its arrowheads. {#strong}⌘D{/strong} duplicates text cards, stickies and frames. {#strong}⌥1{/strong} shows the whole board, {#strong}⌥2{/strong} the selection and {#strong}⌥3{/strong} the live cards; {#strong}⇧⌘F{/strong} fills the view with the board, and {#strong}⌘B{/strong} folds the player and the tray out of its way.
command_guide_tools_arrange: The key at the toolbar's foot arranges the board by beat: a frame for each planned beat in plan order, with the notes several beats share in a frame of their own, Throughout. Once a beat has its frame, launching it shows that frame.
command_guide_images_desc: A note shows the images it embeds, {#em}![[map.png]]{/em} as Obsidian writes them ({#em}![[map.png|300]]{/em} sets the width), on its card and when you read it. Drop an image from Finder on the board to put it there; it's copied into the campaign's {#em}Shelf{/em} folder, so the campaign keeps everything it uses.
command_guide_images_beat: An image in a track or on the shelf works as a note does: put it in a beat, play it, and its card shows it. Double-click it to see it in the inspector. An image isn't spent: spend the beat that shows it.
command_guide_images_tracks: A track holds notes or images, chosen when you insert it: {#em}+ track{/em}, or a track's right-click, offers {#em}Insert note track{/em} ({#strong}⌘T{/strong}) and {#em}Insert image track{/em} ({#strong}⇧⌘T{/strong}). Double-clicking an image track's empty row copies pictures from your Mac into it, as does dropping them on it from Finder; dropped on the shelf, they land there. An image goes only in an image track, and a note only in a note track; the shelf holds both. A new campaign starts with {#em}Maps{/em}, an image track, and a folder of images you fill in Finder is an image track already. In Legend Lore's tree, right-click an image and {#em}Send to Command{/em} to copy it in.
command_guide_session_desc: The bar in the board's corner writes a line into the session note, and {#strong}⌘J{/strong} puts the caret in it, and {#strong}⇧⌘J{/strong} opens the note.
command_settings_load_error: Could not load Command's settings — is the sidecar running? ({error})
command_settings_folder_desc: Each campaign is a folder in here. Changing the folder closes the open campaign and opens a fresh Untitled in the new one — nothing is moved.
command_settings_play_desc: How Command keeps track of a session at the table.
command_settings_spend_desc: Launching a beat marks it spent, so later sessions find it among the spent beats, not those still to play. Off, you tick beats off by hand.
servant_guide_intro: An AI agent that speaks MCP can search your Legend Lore library and read and write your Command campaigns. Help → Reference lists its tools.
servant_guide_paste: Paste it into the agent's MCP settings (inside its {#em}mcpServers{/em} if others are listed) and restart the agent. Keep Unseen Servant running; closing its window doesn't quit it.
servant_guide_scope: The agent searches the whole library unless it names a collection: what plays here doesn't scope it. What its tools return goes to the agent's model, which may run in the cloud; the PDFs themselves stay here.
servant_panel_purpose: An assistant over your library and sessions — not built yet.
